items.title: Fearing stalkers and violent exes, Korean women are hiring their own bodyguards
items.title_zh: 由于害怕跟踪者和暴力前男友，韩国女性正在雇佣自己的保镖
items.summary: After a series of women in Korea were killed after experiencing stalking, assault and threats from former partners or husbands, some potential victims are turning to private bodyguards to protect themselves. They are paying substantial sums out of pocket amid concerns that public protection measures, including emergency smartwatches and restraining orders, may not be enough to keep an attacker away. The government also provides private security services to some crime victims, but funding has failed to keep pace with rapidly growing demand. A 29-year-old woman living in North Jeolla Province, identified only as A, hired a bodyguard for four days in mid-October because her former boyfriend, identified as B, was about to be released from prison. B had served six months in prison for fraud-related offenses, including taking out loans in A's name. Her fears soon became reality. On the second day of the security assignment, B showed up at A's apartment complex. The bodyguard stopped him, warned him not to return and sent him away. items.summary: As online gambling increasingly draws young people into its orbit, casino operator Paradise is putting its money behind a campaign urging teenagers to find a different kind of excitement — one built around their ambitions rather than bets. Paradise said Friday it had fully funded the production of a youth gambling prevention advertisement in partnership with the Korea Center on Gambling Problems, with the video set to debut on television and online platforms at the end of October. Titled “I play a different game,” the campaign carries a message encouraging teenagers to turn away from online gambling and pursue a wider world of opportunities, dreams and personal potential. The advertisement aims to communicate the risks of gambling in language and imagery tailored to younger audiences while raising public awareness of the issue. items.title: Seoul converts underused section of subway station into sports lounge

items.summary: Seoul has turned an underused underground subway concourse into a recreational hub where outdoor runners can change clothes and store gear before hitting nearby riverside trails, while park golf enthusiasts can play indoors regardless of the weather. The facility — the ninth in a municipal network curiously named "Fun Stations" — opened Friday on basement level 1 of Shinmokdong Station on Line 9, offering direct access to the adjacent Anyangcheon stream running paths. The facility, located near exits 1 and 2 on the station's basement level, features a 213-square-meter runner support area and a 228-square-meter indoor park golf center equipped with six screen-based hitting bays. The runner facilities include three changing rooms for men and women each, along with 14 lockers in each section, and are available free of charge. Lockers cost 3,000 won ($2.10) for four hours, while vending machines offer running essentials such as shower wipes and energy gels. items.summary: A researcher and a student from Kookmin University have each received an award at the 2026 Sustainable Smart City Champions Session, the university said. The event was part of Smart Life Week 2026, co-hosted by the World Smart Sustainable Cities Organization (WeGO) and the Seoul Metropolitan Government at Coex in southern Seoul from Oct. 6-8. Ra Min-su, a researcher at the university’s Global Development Cooperation Institute, and Ji Ye-jun, a senior at the Kookmin International Business School, won the 2026 WeGO Global Youth Award on Oct. 7. Ji is also a student supporter of the university’s HUSS (Humanities and Social Sciences) Global Symbiosis Project. WeGO is an international organization that promotes smart and sustainable urban development through cooperation among local governments, businesses and other relevant organizations around the world. items.title: Appellate sentencing in Yoon's high-stakes election law case to be broadcast live

items.summary: Next week's sentencing hearing for former President Yoon Suk Yeol over election law violation charges will be broadcast live, court officials said Friday, a high-stakes ruling that could force the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) to return nearly $30 million in reimbursed election expenses. The Seoul High Court decided to allow broadcasters to air the sentencing scheduled for 2 p.m. Wednesday, officials said. Yoon was sentenced by a district court in July to a 18-month prison term, suspended for three years, for making false statements during the campaign ahead of the March 2022 presidential election that he ultimately won as the PPP's candidate. Yoon was charged with falsely claiming during a December 2021 press event that he had never introduced a lawyer to a former tax official, who is the older brother of former senior prosecutor Yoon Dae-jin, a close associate of Yoon from his time in the prosecution service. items.title: Sejong University professor to co-organize int'l workshop on AI chip technologies in Athens
items.title_zh: 世宗大学教授将在雅典共同举办人工智能芯片技术国际研讨会
items.summary: Park Gi-ho, a professor in the Department of Computer Sciences and Engineering at Sejong University, will co-organize the Eighth International Workshop on Domain Specific System Architecture in Athens, Greece, Sunday. The university said the workshop is part of the 59th IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Microarchitecture (MICRO 2026), which is scheduled to run from Oct. 31 to Nov. 4 in Athens. The workshop aims to share the latest research advances in artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductors and domain-specific system architecture and promote research collaboration among experts from academia and industry worldwide. Key topics will include systematic design methodologies for AI accelerators, programming environments for next-generation neural processing units and memory technologies for robotic foundation models. The workshop is co-organized by Park, professor Sim Jae-woong of Seoul National University and professor Kim Hye-soon of the Georgia Institute of Technology. items.title: Seoul to take necessary measures based on 'clear principles' over DMZ: security adviser
items.title_zh: 首尔将根据有关非军事区的“明确原则”采取必要措施：安全顾问
items.summary: South Korea will continue taking necessary measures based on clear principles in response to the recent mine blast in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), the country's top security adviser said Friday, reiterating the government's focus on establishing peace that eliminates the need for fighting. National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac made the remarks at a press briefing following the detonation of North Korean land mines inside the DMZ in September that wounded three South Korean soldiers, two of them seriously. "Our government will continue taking necessary measures in response to the DMZ mine blast incident based on clear principles," Wi said. "The government will focus its resources on creating peace that makes fighting unnecessary by consistently pursuing its policy of peaceful coexistence," he added. The security adviser said that, since the incident, Seoul has demanded an apology from North Korea, removed mines at the accident site and ensured the military's readiness by test-firing a hypersonic missile. items.title: Special counsel appeals Seoul mayor's acquittal in political funds case

items.summary: A special counsel team said Friday it has appealed the acquittal of Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon in a political funds case linked to the 2021 mayoral by-election. Special counsel Min Joong-ki's team said it filed the appeal with the Seoul High Court earlier in the day, a week after the appellate court overturned a lower court ruling to acquit the mayor of violating the Political Funds Act. Oh had been indicted on charges of having a political supporter make payments totaling 33 million won ($24,700) for opinion polls he allegedly received on 10 occasions from self-proclaimed power broker Myung Tae-kyun ahead of the 2021 election. The lower court found him partially guilty of the charges and sentenced him to a 10 million-won fine, which, if finalized, would have stripped him of his mayoralty. But the appellate court reversed the conviction, ruling that the only direct evidence for the allegations was Myung's testimony, which it said could not be fully trusted. items.title: Sungkyunkwan University President Yoo reappointed for second term

items.summary: Sungkyunkwan University President Yoo Ji-beom has been reappointed for a second four-year term. The university's board of trustees approved Yoo's reappointment at a meeting Thursday. His new term will run from Jan. 1 through Dec. 31, 2030. The board credited Yoo with strengthening the university's research capabilities and global competitiveness, particularly through improvements in international university rankings. It also highlighted his vision for advancing institutional innovation in the artificial intelligence era. The university rose 19 places to 68th among 2,297 institutions worldwide in the 2027 Times Higher Education World University Rankings, released earlier this month. It ranked third in Korea and first among private universities, extending its streak of annual improvements in the rankings to four consecutive years. The university also ranked among the top five universities in education, research and graduate outcomes in The Korea Times University Rankings. items.title: Defense minister says Hegseth dismissed talk of alliance strains as 'fake news'

items.summary: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul said Friday that U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth had dismissed recent speculation about strains in the Korea-U.S. alliance as “fake news” during their meeting earlier this week. Kang made the remarks to reporters as he arrived at the defense ministry in Seoul after attending the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in the Philippines. Asked whether the two sides had any disagreements, Kang said there were none. “Secretary Hegseth dismissed all the talk going around as ‘fake news,’” Kang said. “And I agree with him.” “I don’t believe such talk can shake the strength of the Korea-U.S. alliance, nor should it,” he added. Kang and Hegseth held their first face-to-face meeting Wednesday in Cebu, Philippines, on the sidelines of ADMM-Plus. The meeting lasted about 40 minutes, longer than the 15 minutes initially scheduled. items.title: Saudi Defense Minister discusses regional security with NATO chief, European counterparts

items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman held telephone talks with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte to discuss military and defense cooperation and coordinate efforts in response to ongoing regional developments.During the call, the two sides reviewed joint coordination regarding the current situation in the region, with a focus on supporting regional and international security and stability.Prince Khalid and Rutte also discussed several issues of mutual interest.Separately, the Saudi defense minister held telephone conversations with Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius and Spanish Defense Minister Margarita Robles to discuss regional developments amid the condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.The calls focused on coordinating efforts between Saudi Arabia and the three countries in response to regional developments and exploring ways to strengthen joint action to support security and stability in the region.Prince Khalid also reviewed bilateral military and defense relations with his Canadian, German and Spanish counterparts, including opportunities to further develop cooperation.During his conversation with McGuinty, Prince Khalid extended his condolences over the deaths of several military personnel in a fire at a military base in Canada's Alberta province.He also wished those injured in the incident a speedy recovery.

items.summary: RIYADH — Debris from the intercepted ballistic missile injured a Saudi citizen in Riyadh on Thursday, according to the spokesperson of the Civil Defense. The Civil Defense in Riyadh responded to the fall of debris from two ballistic missiles after they were intercepted and destroyed. The missiles had been launched by the Houthi terrorist militia. The incident resulted in minor injuries to a citizen and material damage to a house and a vehicle, the spokesperson said. In an earlier statement, Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, said that Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh.

items.title: Spanish PM affirms full solidarity with Saudi Arabia during call with Crown Prince
items.title_zh: 西班牙总理在与王储通话期间重申全力声援沙特阿拉伯
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman held a phone call on Thursday with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.During the call, the Crown Prince extended his condolences over the victims of the train collision in Spain. He wished the injured a speedy recovery. Sánchez thanked the Crown Prince for his kind sentiments. The Spanish prime minister also expressed Spain's condemnation of the hostile attacks launched by the Houthi militia against Saudi territories. He affirmed Spain's full solidarity with Saudi Arabia. During the call, the leaders also discussed bilateral relations between the two friendly countries and ways to strengthen them across various fields. Also on Thursday, the Crown Prince held a phone call with President of Romania Nicușor Dan. They discussed the latest regional and international developments. The leaders reviewed bilateral cooperation between the two countries across various sectors and ways to strengthen it.

items.title: Korean President condemns Houthi attacks in call with Saudi Crown Prince
items.title_zh: 韩国总统谴责胡塞武装袭击沙特王储
items.summary: RIYADH — Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman held a phone call on Thursday with President Lee Jae Myung of the Republic of Korea. During the call, the Korean president expressed his country's condemnation of the Houthi militia attacks targeting civilian facilities in Saudi Arabia. The leaders also discussed bilateral relations between the two friendly countries and ways to further develop them in a number of fields.

items.title: Saudi, Yemeni FMs discuss continued Houthi attacks on civilians in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特、也门调频台讨论胡塞武装在电话中继续袭击平民
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan received on Thursday a phone call from Yemeni Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Dr. Afrah Al-Zouba. During the call, the ministers reviewed bilateral relations between the two countries. They discussed the latest developments in Yemen, including the terrorist Houthi militia's continued attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. The ministers also reviewed the efforts to support the Yemeni government in carrying out its duties to strengthen security and stability and ease the suffering of the Yemeni people.

items.title: Commercial Transactions Law strengthens contractual stability, safeguards commercial practices
items.title_zh: 《商业交易法》加强合同稳定性，保障商业惯例
items.summary: RIYADH —The Commercial Transactions Law keeps pace with developments in the commercial and investment environment through its comprehensive scope and consistency with laws that promote contractual stability and enforceability and protect the interests of parties to commercial transactions. It complements the Civil Transactions Law. The Commercial Transactions Law stipulates that the provisions of the Civil Transactions Law apply to cases not expressly addressed by the former when no commercial custom or practice exists, making the Civil Transactions Law a supplementary source for filling legislative gaps in the commercial environment. In establishing certain provisions, the law also relies on general rules codified in the Civil Transactions Law to address matters for which no specific commercial provisions exist. The Commercial Transactions Law, which governs commercial transactions, draws on the terminology and theoretical framework set out in the draft Civil Transactions Law to ensure consistency and harmony between the two laws. The Commercial Transactions Law also addresses commercial contracts and commercial agencies, which had not previously been governed by detailed legislation. It establishes clear procedures and rules for commercial contracts and agencies to promote transparency and fairness in commercial dealings and protect the rights of contracting parties. These matters are covered by approximately 69 of the law's 271 articles. The law sets out the rules and requirements governing commercial sales, supply contracts, commercial agencies, and brokerage, addressing the obligations of all parties and the consequences of breaching agreed terms.

items.title: King Salman appoints Sheikh Al-Maiouf deputy head of Board of Grievances
items.title_zh: 萨勒曼国王任命Sheikh Al-Maiouf为申诉委员会副主任
items.summary: RIYADH —Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman has issued a royal decree appointing Sheikh Abdulmohsen Al-Maiouf as deputy head of the Board of Grievances for judicial affairs.Dr. Al-Maiouf is a distinguished judicial and administrative figure with academic qualifications and extensive experience. He holds a doctorate degree in Islamic jurisprudence and comparative law.Sheikh Al-Maiouf has advanced through various positions within the Board of Grievances, serving in administrative and commercial departments and administrative appeals courts before eventually assuming the presidency of the Technical Affairs Office.He has also served on numerous supervisory and governmental committees. He made outstanding contributions in the field of reviewing draft laws, regulations, and agreements, and participated in legal conferences and forums at both the Saudi and international levels. Sheikh Al-Maiouf expressed his gratitude to King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman on the occasion of his appointment. He expressed pride over this esteemed royal trust reposed in him, saying that this represents both an honor and a responsibility in serving the administrative judiciary. “This trust motivates me to continue working to enhance the efficiency of judicial work, develop its procedures, and strengthen its integration, in line with the objectives of the Board of Grievances system for leadership and maximizing its impact,” he said.

items.title: Saudi Arabia offers condolences to Spain over train crash
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯就火车事故向西班牙表示哀悼
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Foreign Affairs extended Saudi Arabia's condolences to the families of the victims as well as to the government and people of Spain over the train collision in Toledo province that caused deaths and injuries. "Saudi Arabia expresses its solidarity with the government and people of Spain in the wake of this tragic incident, wishing a speedy recovery to those injured, and safety and security for Spain and its friendly people," the ministry said in a statement.At least 69 people were killed and over 100 others injured after a high-speed Renfe train rear-ended a stationary Iryo train on the Madrid–Seville line near Urda in central Spain on Wednesday.

items.title: Licensed worker housing mandatory for establishments with fewer than 250 employees from Feb. 1, 2027
items.title_zh: 自2027年2月1日起，员工人数少于250人的企业必须提供有执照的工人住房
items.summary: RIYADH —The National Program for Developing Group Housing for Individuals has stressed the importance of establishments with fewer than 250 targeted employees regularizing their worker accommodation and meeting all regulatory requirements ahead of the final phase of mandatory implementation, which begins on February 1, 2027. The program, chaired by the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing, regulates worker accommodations across Saudi Arabia to ensure health, safety, and quality-of-life standards. The measure includes complying with the applicable regulations and providing licensed group housing, as part of efforts to regulate worker accommodation and improve the quality of the residential environment in the cities across Saudi Arabia.The program clarified that the remaining period before the requirement takes effect constitutes a grace period, allowing establishments sufficient time to complete the necessary procedures. The program reaffirmed its commitment to supporting establishments and helping them regularize their status through approved regulatory channels, ensuring compliance and readiness for implementation. It explained that establishments can regularize their worker accommodation through one of two approved options. The first is to obtain a shared accommodation license for the establishment’s building through approved licensing platforms, after meeting the prescribed health, technical, and safety requirements. The second is to enter into contracts with pre-licensed shared accommodation units, enabling establishments to provide regulated housing for their employees without having to operate their own residential facilities. The program underscored the importance of completing licensing procedures or contracting with licensed accommodation providers without delay and within the grace period. It noted that compliance with the approved options would help regulate worker accommodation, strengthen adherence to health, technical, and safety standards, and curb the unauthorized use of residential buildings. The program explained that regulating shared accommodation aims to provide suitable living conditions that meet health and safety standards, enhance quality of life, and improve the urban landscape, while striking a balance between enabling establishments to carry out their activities and ensuring compliance with the regulations governing worker accommodation. The program urged eligible establishments to make full use of the grace period by completing the required procedures through approved platforms or selecting licensed accommodation units to avoid potential legal consequences for non-compliance, in accordance with the approved regulations and guidelines.It is worthy to note that several ministries and government agencies have membership in the National Program for Developing Group Housing for Individuals, headed by the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing.
